cases.title: Maya writes PHI policy in English. Wrapbox won't overclaim.
cases.why: A HIPAA audit asks how PHI in scanned attachments is stopped before it reaches external AI.

steps.ui: Click + Draft contract, type the rule in plain English
steps.system: Drafter drawer holds name + sourceText; nothing compiled yet (intent-studio.tsx)

steps.ui: Click Compile, read the clause preview
steps.system: draftClauses(text) splits sentences, extracts dataClasses, effect, transform, destinations, requiredCapabilities

steps.ui: Click Save as draft
steps.system: coverageRollup(preview) sets coverage; upsertContract() stores it as DRAFT v1

steps.ui: Open the contract card, inspect required skills
steps.system: contractCoverage() = worst capability status; UNINSPECTABLE 'Encrypted content' counts as PENDING

steps.ui: Click Activate
steps.system: Button disabled; setContractStatus(id,'ACTIVE') returns false because canActivate() is false

codePath: brain.decide() reads only contracts where status === 'ACTIVE'
cases.outcome: The PHI contract exists as a DRAFT with honest PENDING coverage; it is not enforced and Wrapbox tells Maya exactly which skill is missing.
cases.evidence: Contract status/version/coverage live in the store: Intent Studio card + drawer, Coverage Map 'inactive' row (Draft — not switched on) and 'gap' row for Encrypted content; no evidence-chain event is written by drafting or activation.
cases.realVsSimulated: draftClauses() is a deterministic keyword/regex compiler standing in for the product's Policy IR; coverage rollup, the activation guard and decide() consuming only ACTIVE contracts are real logic over the static CAPABILITIES registry; new drafts are stamped author u-priya regardless of who is signed in.

cases.title: Claude Code reaches for .env. Daniel sees why it stopped.
cases.why: Claude Code, debugging a config issue on his laptop, runs `cat .env`; Daniel wants to know why it stopped.

steps.ui: Opens Simulation Lab, Endpoint tab, picks "Agent reads .env", presses Run
steps.system: sim-lab start() calls store simulate(sc); the event is real and recorded

steps.ui: Watches the agent terminal reveal Bash(cat .env) stage by stage
steps.system: runScenario() builds ActionRequest (SECRET_ACCESS, CREDENTIAL.* findings via buildInspection); decide() matches cl-eng-2 → BLOCK

steps.ui: Reads "Decision: BLOCK · Decided by …" and "Blocked before execution"
steps.system: pipelineFor() emits stages; AgentTerminal linesFor() derives every line from the event

steps.ui: Opens Live Actions; the blocked row is newest
steps.system: store set() appended the event to s.events; LiveActions renders s.events through EventStream, metrics() counts BLOCK

steps.ui: Opens Core Brain to see which gate objected
steps.system: CoreBrainPage decided('contract') counts events by decidedBy.layer; "Your rules" gets the credit

codePath: runScenario(sc, state.contracts, state.lastHash, { breakGlass: bg, kernel: state.kernel, standing: state.standing })
cases.outcome: The secret read never executes: decision BLOCK, status blocked, decidedBy "Agents must not read local secrets files" (Engineering guardrails), safer path offered.
cases.evidence: One SimulationEvent (evt-NNNNN) with chain User→Agent→Tool→Action→Resource→Findings→Rules matched→Decided by→Decision→Enforcement and a hash; shown in Simulation Lab terminal, Live Actions, Evidence, Core Brain, Control Room.
cases.realVsSimulated: The Claude Code session, the .env read and its CREDENTIAL findings are scripted scenario data (no file is read, no agent runs); clause matching, precedence, decidedBy, the hash chain and store propagation to every page are real code.

cases.title: A force-push to main is parked. Alex decides in seconds.
cases.why: Daniel's Claude Code ran `git push --force origin main` in production; the brain parked it as REVIEW.

steps.ui: Daniel's agent fires the force-push (Simulation Lab / Tasks)
steps.system: store.simulate() → runScenario() → decide(); clause cl-eng-3 (WRITE, SOURCE_CODE, production) returns REVIEW

steps.ui: Event lands as pending with a 4-hour expiry
steps.system: runScenario() sets reviewState {status:'pending', expiresAt: ts+4h, safeAlternative} and status 'pending_review'

steps.ui: Alex opens Review Center → Awaiting your decision
steps.system: approverFor(e) routes to task approver or Engineering Manager, never e.user (requester)

steps.ui: Alex reads why, blast radius (31 files, 14 commits), safer alternative
steps.system: Card renders e.decisionReasons[0], e.blastRadius, e.safeAlternative from suggestAlternative(): feature branch + PR

steps.ui: Alex clicks Approve once / Approve scoped / Constrain / Deny
steps.system: resolveReview() stamps reviewer, decidedAt, scope; appends Review + Outcome to evidence chain once

cases.outcome: The event is completed (approved), transformed (constrained) or blocked (denied); a denial stays denied and an approval never widens later scope.
cases.evidence: reviewState {status, reviewer, scope, decidedAt} plus Review/Outcome chain entries; shown in Review Center → Resolved, Evidence → Human review column, and the event's Full evidence drawer.
cases.realVsSimulated: Real: decide() clause matching, requester/approver separation, 4h expiry, state mutation and evidence chain. Simulated: the git push itself, GitHub MCP, and the hash chain; no permit id exists in this prototype (that lives in the main app).

cases.title: customers.csv goes to the AI. The emails and phones don't.
cases.why: Priya attaches customers.csv to the approved enterprise AI and clicks Send to draft renewal emails.

steps.ui: Pick "Customer PII → approved AI" in Simulation Lab, press Run
steps.system: store.simulate(sc) → runScenario(); buildInspection() yields PII.NAME/EMAIL/PHONE via csv-parser-v2

steps.ui: Watch the pipeline reach Core Brain evaluation
steps.system: decide() matches clause cl-ai-2 (External AI usage): CONSTRAIN, transform REVERSIBLE_TOKENIZE, strictest wins

steps.ui: Read "What left the device" in the event detail
steps.system: applyTransform() regex-swaps emails/phones for EMAIL_TOKEN_nnn; VaultTokens appended to store.tokens

steps.ui: Open Token Vault, pick the token, click Restore as inside and outside
steps.system: restoreToken() allows only inside && restorable && !expired; every attempt appended to restorations

steps.ui: Check the decision mix in Live Actions, then the Restore log tab in Token Vault
steps.system: metrics() counts the CONSTRAIN event; EventDetail links payloadAfter to Token Vault

cases.outcome: The AI receives customers.csv with 6 tokens instead of 3 emails and 3 phones; originals never left the device, and only an inside requester can restore them.
cases.evidence: A CONSTRAIN event (status transformed, chain hash, before/after payload) in Live Actions and Evidence; 6 VaultTokens in Token Vault contents; each RestoreRecord (allowed/denied, reason) in the Restore log.
cases.realVsSimulated: Real: clause matching in decide(), regex tokenization, vault entries, restore authorization and log on live store state. Simulated: the Network Extension intercept, detector findings from scenario fixtures (not a real CSV parser), in-memory vault, and inside/outside requester as a button choice rather than an identity check; PII.NAME is detected but not tokenized.

cases.title: A $1,240 refund parks mid-job. Jordan's agent keeps working.
cases.why: Ticket #4821 is a double charge; Jordan hands the whole fix to the Support Agent, not step by step.

steps.ui: Tasks → Start a task → Start "Resolve refund ticket #4821"
steps.system: startTask("job-sup-refund") boxes Support Agent in the Support slip; advanceTask() runs ready steps

steps.ui: Timeline: step 4 "Refund $1,240" shows PARKED; reply and close wait
steps.system: advanceTask → runScenario → decide(): blastGovernor $1,240 > $20 → REVIEW, routed to approver Sam

steps.ui: Sam opens Review Center and clicks Approve once (or Approve scoped)
steps.system: resolveReview() appends Review/Outcome to the evidence chain; resumeParkedStep() re-runs advanceTask()

steps.ui: Standing Permissions: Support Agent on customer-db (≤500 rows) → Revoke
steps.system: revokeStanding("sp-002"); impact computed by shadowEvaluate() shows which ALLOWs would become REVIEW

steps.ui: Click "Grant again for 7 days"
steps.system: grantStandingAgain() sets status active, expiresAt +7d; decide() step 7b enforces lapsed/deny/maxRows outside tasks

cases.outcome: Refund step executes only after Sam's yes, dependents resume automatically, task completes; Support Agent's everyday customer-db authority is off until re-granted, then active for 7 days.
cases.evidence: Every step is a hash-chained SimulationEvent (taskId, stepIndex, decidedBy); approval appends Review + Outcome chain entries — visible in Tasks timeline (click step), Review Center, Live Actions, Evidence. Revoke/grant updates s.standing (status, grantedBy, expiresAt) on Standing Permissions only, not as an event.
cases.realVsSimulated: Real: envelope scope/forbidden/time/file-budget checks, blast-radius $20 spend limit, park → approve → resume with dependency gating, and standing lapsed/deny/maxRows checks all run through decide(). Simulated: the Stripe refund, SQL lookups, Support SaaS calls and the agent itself never leave the browser; the hash chain is an in-page simpleHash.

cases.title: SEV-1 at 2am. Alex breaks glass for one system, 20 minutes.
cases.why: Checkout is down; the hotfix deploy is parked in REVIEW and no approver is awake.

steps.ui: Open Break Glass; type reason (min 8 chars), pick AWS Production, set 20 min
steps.system: startBreakGlass() records scopeResource r-aws-prod + scopeEnvironment production, clamps 5–60 min, notifies u-maya/u-alex (minus requester)

steps.ui: Run 'Deploy checkout hotfix to production' in Simulation Lab
steps.system: store.simulate() passes activeBreakGlass() scope into runScenario() → decide()

steps.ui: Watch the parked deploy go through
steps.system: decide() step 9: in-scope REVIEW with no Safety Kernel hit becomes ALLOW, decidedBy.layer = "breakglass"; simulate.ts stamps event.breakGlass = true

steps.ui: Run 'DELETE production payment database' while the override is live
steps.system: Resource is r-payments-prod, not r-aws-prod → inScope false, override never applies; Safety Kernel 'Destructive production mutation' keeps BLOCK — and would even under a payments-prod override (safety.length > 0)

steps.ui: Click 'End override now'
steps.system: endBreakGlass() sets active:false; history card shows Ended and 'Overrode N actions'

cases.outcome: The hotfix deploy executed under emergency authority; the destructive DELETE of payments-prod stayed BLOCK (out of scope, and kernel-protected regardless); the override is ended and retained forever.
cases.evidence: BreakGlassSession in store.breakGlass (History cards; Active overrides / Lifetime activations / Expired-ended metrics); each overridden event stamped breakGlass:true → BREAK-GLASS chip and 'Break-glass' tally on Evidence, and 'Overridden under this session' list on Break Glass.
cases.realVsSimulated: Real: scope match, kernel precedence, time-box expiry, stamping and hash-chained evidence all run through decide(). Simulated: no sign-in, so the page passes "u-priya" as requester (Alex appears as notified); notifications are recorded, not sent; deploys are scenario objects, not AWS calls.

cases.title: New kernel rule. Priya installs it without breaking anyone.
cases.why: Safety Kernel shows "Update available" — Wrapbox released v2026.09.2 adding Protected history rewrite.

steps.ui: Opens Safety Kernel; reads the v2026.09.2 release notes and 'Impact on your history'
steps.system: pendingRelease(kernel) finds the release; wouldChange() replays r.test(factsFromEvent(e)) over past non-BLOCK events

steps.ui: Clicks Install update
steps.system: installKernelUpdate() → installRelease() sets sk-history-rewrite to observing, observeUntil = now + OBSERVE_WINDOW_DAYS

steps.ui: Runs Force push main from Simulation Lab
steps.system: simulate(sc) → runScenario() → decide() → kernelHits(): hit lands in safetyObserved; decision stays REVIEW, reason says 'would have blocked this'

steps.ui: Clicks Start enforcing now on the observing rule card
steps.system: enforceKernelRule() → enforceRule() flips mode to enforcing, deletes observeUntil

steps.ui: Runs the same force push again
steps.system: kernelHits() returns an enforced hit; decide() forces BLOCK, decidedBy layer 'safety'

cases.outcome: Kernel is v2026.09.2 with 7 rules; force-push over main is BLOCKed by the kernel regardless of any company contract. Kernel rules cannot be switched off, and even an active Break Glass does not override a kernel hit — decide() only applies break-glass when safety.length === 0.
cases.evidence: Each event stores safetyRules, safetyObserved, decidedBy and a hash-chained evidence record; Safety Kernel shows per-rule Fired / Decided / Would have blocked counts and a 'Where they fired' list, Live Actions and Evidence show the same events, and Coverage Map's 'Always-on safety' tab lists the installed kernel rules.
cases.realVsSimulated: Real: install/observe/enforce state machine, effectiveMode auto-enforce after 7 days, replay over history, and decide() precedence are genuine logic; simulated: the Wrapbox update channel is a hard-coded KERNEL_RELEASES list, not a network feed, and the force push is a scenario, not a real git gateway.

cases.title: Priya sees which promises Wrapbox can actually keep
cases.why: Integrations shows a connection "Understood only"; she must know which written rules that weakens before claiming compliance.

steps.ui: Opens Integrations, scans the enforcement strip
steps.system: statusOf(connection) takes the worst live skill in c.caps from CAPABILITIES (PENDING skills listed but not counted); MetricBar tallies Enforced / Degraded / Understood only

steps.ui: Clicks "Understood only" — lands on Coverage Map
steps.system: nav("coverage"); buildCoverageMatrix(s.contracts, s.kernel) derives rules, safety, gaps, inactive rows and counts live

steps.ui: Reads "Your rules": each clause lists the skills it needs
steps.system: ruleRow → clauseCoverage(cl) → coverageOf() takes the worst status across cl.requiredCapabilities

steps.ui: Opens "Known gaps": MCP gateway is Understood only but holds back 0 rules; Semantic classification (Degraded) shows "2 rules" — she clicks it
steps.system: gaps = CAPABILITIES not ENFORCED, sorted by affected rules+safety; jump("rules", g) filters Your rules to clauses needing that skill

steps.ui: In Intent Studio tries to activate "PHI handling (draft)" — Activate is disabled: Encrypted content cannot be inspected
steps.system: contractCoverage(contract) === "PENDING" (UNINSPECTABLE → PENDING) disables the button; setContractStatus() also returns false when !canActivate(target)

cases.outcome: Every live promise carries the status of its weakest skill; a contract whose skill is PENDING or uninspectable cannot be activated, so coverage is never over-claimed.
cases.evidence: No event is written — coverage is recomputed from CAPABILITIES; contractCoverage() is stored on each IntentContract and shows as the Coverage chip in Intent Studio, the posture bar/tabs in Coverage Map, and the Enforced/Degraded/Understood-only strip in Integrations.
cases.realVsSimulated: Real: coverageOf/contractCoverage/canActivate ranking, matrix derivation, gap sorting, activation guard and cross-page consistency. Simulated: the skill statuses in CAPABILITIES and every connection/rollout (GitHub, AWS, SQL, MCP) are demo data, not live integrations.

cases.title: An auditor asks "prove it." Maya opens the chained ledger.
cases.why: Audit asks who approved last night's code export and whether the log could have been edited.

steps.ui: Open Evidence; read the chain head and counts
steps.system: EvidenceExplorer renders store.lastHash and tallies BLOCK/REVIEW/break-glass from s.events

steps.ui: Filter Decision=REVIEW, Human review=Approved (scoped)
steps.system: useCardFilters searches describe(e), dataClasses, matchedContracts clauseText; each card shows hash ← prevHash

steps.ui: Click the export event; open Causal graph
steps.system: EventDetail + EvidenceChain render evidence.chain built in runScenario(); Review/Outcome nodes appended by resolveReview()

steps.ui: Cross-check the same id under Review Center → Resolved
steps.system: Review Center 'Resolved' section (metric 'Decided') lists the same SimulationEvent (e.id, reviewState.reviewer, reviewState.decidedAt)

steps.ui: Open Trust Graph, click the agent node
steps.system: TrustGraph derives user→agent→destination edges from s.events; risky edges/stranger nodes highlighted

cases.outcome: Maya can show an unbroken hash chain from genesis0 to the chain head, with the reviewer, scope and time on the exact event the Review Center resolved.
cases.evidence: Each SimulationEvent carries evidence {eventId, hash, prevHash, chain}; shown on Evidence cards/graph, EventDetail drawer, Review Center 'Resolved', and as edges in Trust Graph.
cases.realVsSimulated: Real: chain built per event, hash = FNV-1a over prev+id+decision+ts, store advances lastHash, review resolution appends chain nodes, graph derived from events. Simulated: FNV-1a in-browser stands in for a signed ledger; there is no separate permit id — the Review Center ticket IS the event id.

cases.title: Priya sets up Wrapbox from zero. Every page fills itself in.
cases.why: A new company has agents already running and no governance; Priya must go live before anyone else joins.

steps.ui: Opens Get started, starts a fresh workspace
steps.system: startFreshWorkspace() loads freshState(); wizard session keys cleared, checklist all unticked

steps.ui: Enters company, domain, SSO, data region; clicks Create
steps.system: makeSigningKey() runs crypto.subtle.generateKey(ECDSA P-256); setOrg() stores keyThumb + createdAt

steps.ui: Scans repos, ticks agent kinds, publishes recommended contracts
steps.system: setOnboarding({categories}); publishRecommendedContracts() activates only contracts canActivate() can keep

steps.ui: Connects endpoint, network and gateways one by one
steps.system: connect() plays vendor phases, then setOnboarding({connected}); rolloutStatus() reads CAPABILITIES registry

steps.ui: Runs three go-live self-tests, clicks Finish
steps.system: simulateById() → runScenario() → decide(); setOnboarding({selfTests}); completeAdminOnboarding(); nav("control")

codePath: setOrg({company, domain, region, idp, keyThumb, createdAt})
start.tsx checklist(s) derives 8 milestones from org / contracts / onboarding / events
cases.outcome: The workspace has a signed identity, governed agent kinds, active contracts, connected planes, an invited team and its first real decisions; onboarding.adminDone is true.
cases.evidence: org.keyThumb, onboarding.{categories,connected,invited,selfTests,adminDone}, contracts and hash-chained events land in the store; they surface as Get started checklist ticks, Intent Studio contracts, Integrations status, Live Actions rows, Evidence entries and Control Room counts.
cases.realVsSimulated: Real: the ECDSA P-256 key and SHA-256 thumbprint (WebCrypto), contract activation guard, self-test decisions through decide(), and every checklist/page derived from the one store; simulated: the GitHub repo scan, MDM/gateway rollout phases, SSO directory sync and invite emails.

cases.title: Maya tests a rule change on real history before go-live.
cases.why: A contract change is proposed; Maya must prove what it would allow or weaken before enforcing it.

steps.ui: Open Policy Simulator, tab 1, untick a clause or tick a switched-off contract
steps.system: PolicySimulator builds `proposed` contracts: active minus removed clause ids, plus added ones

steps.ui: Open tab 2, choose Your history or Scenario library
steps.system: shadowEvaluate(sc, s.contracts) and shadowEvaluate(sc, proposed) run decide() per row; nothing recorded

steps.ui: Read the before/after mix and the weakened warning
steps.system: rows where current !== prop are `changed`; prop === ALLOW flags `weakened`, Safety Kernel still applies

steps.ui: In Simulation Lab pick the scenario, press Step through
steps.system: simulate(sc) calls runScenario() → decide(); pipelineFor() reveals stages; event stored with hash chain

steps.ui: Tab 3, Open Intent Studio to make it real
steps.system: nav("intent"); the simulator itself never writes contracts or events

codePath: PolicySimulator proposed (useMemo over s.contracts, removed, added)
SimulationLab start() → simulate(sc) → runScenario(sc, state.contracts, state.lastHash) → set({ events, tokens, lastHash })
cases.outcome: Maya knows exactly which recorded actions flip decision under the proposal, and which protections would be weakened, before any rule changes.
cases.evidence: Policy Simulator records nothing (seq and token counter restored, hash "shadow"); a Simulation Lab run stores a real event that appears in Control Room, Live Actions, Agents, Token Vault and Evidence.
cases.realVsSimulated: Real: same decide() and runScenario() as the runtime, real contract diffing, real seq/token restore; simulated: the scenarios themselves (files, endpoints, processes) are a fixed library, and the matcher here is clauseMatches() inside decide(), not a separate checkRule().
